outline.target_audience: First-year University Calculus Students / Advanced High School Students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Hidden Function
sections.content: Introduce the difference between 'Explicit' functions (y is isolated) and 'Implicit' equations (x and y are tangled). Establish the prerequisite: The Chain Rule. Use a visual metaphor of a 'Gift Box' where 'y' is a package containing an unknown 'x' inside.
sections.example: Explicit: y = x² + 1 (The path is clear). Implicit: x² + y² = 25 (The path is a circle; y is trapped inside the equation).

sections.title: Why Not Just Solve for Y?
sections.content: Demonstrate the 'Pain Point.' Show that isolating 'y' in complex equations often leads to messy square roots or multiple branches, making standard differentiation difficult. Graphically show a circle splitting into two separate functions (top and bottom arcs) to explain why a unified approach is better.
sections.example: Try solving for 'y' in x³ + y³ = 6xy. It results in a mathematical nightmare! We need a way to find the slope without 'untangling' the equation.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Treat Y as y(x)
sections.content: The core conceptual leap. Explain that whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must apply the Chain Rule because 'y' is a function of 'x'. Use an animation of a 'Chain Link' appearing every time 'y' is touched.
sections.example: When differentiating y² with respect to x: Think of it as [f(x)]². The derivative is 2y * (dy/dx). The (dy/dx) is the 'tail' left behind by the Chain Rule.

sections.title: The 3-Step Execution Recipe
sections.content: Provide a logical procedural workflow for solving any implicit problem. Step 1: Differentiate both sides (term by term). Step 2: Group all terms containing 'dy/dx' on the left. Step 3: Factor out 'dy/dx' and solve algebraically. Show this as a mechanical assembly line process.
sections.example: Equation: x² + y² = 25. Step 1: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Step 2: 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Step 3: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Application: The Mechanical Gear
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world shape like an Ellipse or a 'Folium of Descartes' (a loop). Use a 'Robot Arm' character trying to find the exact slope at a specific point on a circular gear to ensure smooth movement. This integrates the algebraic result with a geometric tangent line.
sections.example: Find the slope of the curve x² + xy + y² = 7 at the point (1, 2). Calculate dy/dx and plug in the coordinates to show the slope of the tangent line is -4/5.

sections.title: Summary & Visual Review
sections.content: Quick recap of the 'Chain Rule tail' and the power of implicit differentiation to find slopes of shapes that aren't traditional functions. Ends with a high-speed animation of various curves (hearts, infinity symbols) and their corresponding tangent lines moving along the perimeter.
sections.example: Remember: Every time you derive 'y', multiply by dy/dx. It’s the key that unlocks the geometry of curves!

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Hidden Function
lecture_lines: Some functions isolate y, like y equals x squared.
Others hide y inside, like x squared plus y squared.
Implicit equations keep y tangled with x.
animations: Fade in 'y = x^2 + 1' in green #55FF55; label it 'Explicit'.
Fade in 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' in red #FF5555; label it 'Implicit'.
Circle the 'y' in the implicit equation with yellow #FFFF00 pulsing light.
Replace 'y' with a gold #FFD700 gift box icon to represent hidden x.
Show 'Chain Rule' text in white #FFFFFF above the box.

storyboard.title: Why Not Just Solve for Y?
lecture_lines: Solving for y creates messy, multiple equations.
A circle splits into complex top and bottom halves.
We must derive without untangling the equation first.
animations: Display 'x^3 + y^3 = 6xy' in white #FFFFFF with a red #FF5555 question mark.
Morph equation into a mess of square roots to show difficulty.
Draw a circle #FFFFFF and split it into two halves.
Color top half blue #00AAFF and bottom half orange #FFAA00.
Flash 'Messy Branches' text in red #FF5555.

storyboard.title: The Golden Rule: Treat Y as y(x)
lecture_lines: Treat y as a hidden function of x.
When deriving y, we must use the Chain Rule.
Think of y squared as a package containing x.
The derivative is 2y times the tail, dy/dx.
Every y derivative leaves a dy/dx link behind.
animations: Show 'y' morphing into 'y(x)' in cyan #00FFFF.
Write 'd/dx [ y^2 ]' in white #FFFFFF.
Transform to '2y' followed by an empty 'Chain Link' slot.
Fill the slot with 'dy/dx' in bold gold #FFD700.
Highlight the 'dy/dx' tail with a glowing border.

storyboard.title: The 3-Step Execution Recipe
lecture_lines: Step one: Differentiate every term on both sides.
Step two: Move all dy/dx terms to the left.
Step three: Factor out dy/dx from the group.
Finally, divide to isolate dy/dx on its own.
This mechanical process works for any implicit equation.
animations: Show 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' becoming '2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0' via term-by-term derivation.
Animate the '2x' term moving to the right side of the equation.
Isolate 'dy/dx' on the left and box the final result '-x/y' in green #55FF55.

storyboard.title: Application: The Mechanical Gear
lecture_lines: Let's find the slope on this complex gear curve.
Differentiate the equation term by term.
Group and solve to find the derivative formula.
Plugging in coordinates reveals the exact tangent slope.
This tangent line ensures the gear's smooth movement.
animations: Draw an ellipse 'x^2 + xy + y^2 = 7' in purple #EE82EE.
Place a glowing point at coordinate (1, 2).
Draw a tangent line at (1, 2) and display 'Slope = -4/5' in yellow #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Summary & Visual Review
lecture_lines: Every y derivative needs a dy/dx tail.
Implicit differentiation unlocks geometry for complex curves.
Now you can find slopes for any hidden function.
animations: Display 'y derivative -> add dy/dx' in gold #FFD700 as a summary rule.
Show a heart-shaped curve and an infinity symbol in pink #FFC0CB.
Animate tangent lines rotating around the curves to show the power of the method.
